affectedSurfaces: repo task queue validation ready-coverage evidence
autonomy task-claim filtering for queue coverage
hypothesis: Applying claim-aware ordinary-dispatchability filtering to strategic ready coverage will prevent a pending-merge p1 or p2 ready task from masking a p3-only dispatchable queue, while preserving visibility for claim-blocked tasks and safe-to-retry claims.

metricsCompared.name: pending-merge strategic ready coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: explorer computed strategicReadyCoverageGap from raw task files, so an unclaimable pending-merge p1 or p2 ready task could satisfy coverage even when ordinary dispatchable ready work was p3-only
metricsCompared.candidate: explorer inspect-queue and the strategic-ready-coverage repair check both exclude non-retryable claim-blocked tasks through the autonomy-owned coverage adapter

metricsCompared.name: safe-to-retry and dependency semantics
metricsCompared.baseline: strategic coverage did not share task-claim retry semantics and raw ready/backlog evidence could count dependency-blocked or anchor tasks
metricsCompared.candidate: focused tests cover pending-merge exclusion, expired safe-to-retry strategic claims, ordinary p2 ready work, dependency-blocked ready/backlog tasks, and strategic anchors

metricsCompared.name: local validation
metricsCompared.baseline: task started with a known explorer coverage blind spot and no claim-aware strategic ready coverage adapter
metricsCompared.candidate: focused repo-task, autonomy, dispatcher, builder, task-claim, validate-tasks, typecheck, and lint checks passed with the task moved to done

rationale: The workflow behavior change is narrow and aligns explorer's strategic coverage signal with the existing claim-aware queue snapshot. Repo-tasks keeps a neutral excludedTaskIds option instead of depending on autonomy, and autonomy owns the task-claim filtering. The recorded focused tests cover the pending-merge failure shape, safe retry claims, ordinary strategic work, dependency blockers, and existing queue availability behavior.
